examples.description: Create a new workspace with an auto-generated name
Create a new workspace named 'feature-auth'
Create a workspace and run npm install
Create a workspace and copy environment files
Create a workspace from main branch
Create a workspace from remote branch

notes: If name is omitted, a random human-readable name is generated automatically
The workspace name will be used as the branch name. An existing workspace is refused with exit 4; failures after creation, including metadata, copy, hooks, or --exec, exit 6

When the name is already a branch on a configured remote, create exits 4 and tells you to run mabo attach <name>. It does not fetch. A workspace that already exists is still reported as already existing.
Gitignored files matching .worktreeinclude at the checkout root are copied into the new workspace
.worktreeinclude and --copy-file use gitignore syntax. A file is copied only when it matches and is gitignored, so tracked files are never duplicated
Files that already exist in the new workspace are left unchanged
Symlinks are skipped and are not followed. A .worktreeinclude symlink is not read
.mabo.toml is read from the source checkout, the checkout where the command runs. [hooks] post-create commands run in the new workspace, in order, and stop at the first failure

post-create hooks run only after the repository is trusted. On a terminal, mabo shows the project path and the hook commands and asks 'Trust this project and run its hooks? [y/N]'. No, a non-terminal, stdin or stderr not being a terminal, nonempty CI, --no-input or MABO_NO_INPUT being enabled, or --json fails before creating the workspace. An empty value counts as unset. Run mabo trust --yes or pass --no-hooks. MABO_TRUST_ALL=1 trusts every repository for that process and writes nothing

Hooks and exec receive MABO=1, MABO_WORKSPACE (the workspace name), MABO_WORKSPACE_ID (the ws_ ID, or empty if unrecorded), MABO_WORKSPACE_PATH (the absolute workspace path), and MABO_REPO_PATH (the primary checkout path)
--json writes the workspace object, copyFiles, and postCreate outcome to stdout. The schema is documented in the README

New workspaces are created under $XDG_DATA_HOME/maboroshi/workspaces/<checkout>-<hash> (default ~/.local/share/maboroshi/workspaces/...). <checkout> is the canonical primary checkout directory name, so a symlink uses the same directory. <hash> is the first 8 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the canonical Git common directory. A relative XDG_DATA_HOME is ignored. worktrees-directory overrides this and is joined to the repository root

Owner, purpose, and links are stored in maboroshi/workspaces/<id>.json under the Git common directory. --owner overrides MABO_AGENT_ID. Omit both to leave the owner empty. where and exec refresh lastUsedAt

All JSON uses schema 2: {schema:2, command, ok, data, warnings:[{code,message}], error:null|{code,message,details?}}. data preserves partial results and has no top-level version/schema. Parsers must ignore unknown fields. Exit codes: 0 success, 1 operational failure, 2 usage/ambiguous, 3 not found/not repository, 4 safety refusal (dirty/unpreserved/published/exists/exists_remote/untrusted; refused when the cause is unknown), 5 sync conflict, 6 partial persistent changes. Standalone exec preserves child statuses

Delete multiple workspaces in one command

notes: An orphaned record (no Git registration and no directory) is removed without hooks or branch changes. A live match takes precedence. JSON reports workspace.orphaned: true and branchDeleted: false
By default, deletion will fail if the workspace has uncommitted changes

By default, deletion will fail if the branch has commits that are not on the default branch or any remote, or if that check cannot be completed. --keep-branch still deletes the workspace and leaves the branch
Deleting the workspace that contains the current directory requires --current or --force
You can pass multiple workspace names to delete them at once. A safety refusal exits 4 before deleting any workspace. Later failures exit 6 if a persistent removal occurred, otherwise 1

gc.name: gc

options.name: project
options.description: Repository to operate on instead of the current directory. It may appear with the other options. A value starting with /, ., or ~ is a directory inside the repository, including a linked workspace, and resolves to the primary checkout. Any other value matches a known project's canonical host/owner/repo name, the directory name from project list, or an unambiguous suffix such as owner/repo or repo

options.name: apply
options.description: Remove the workspaces the dry run would remove. Without --apply or --force, gc only prints the plan

options.name: force
options.description: Remove matching workspaces even when they are dirty or have unpushed commits. Implies --apply. Does not remove the current workspace, a locked workspace, or another agent's workspace that matched only on age

options.name: merged
options.description: Select workspaces whose branch is contained in the default branch. With no criterion flag, merged, closed pull requests, and orphaned workspaces are all selected

options.name: pr
options.description: Select workspaces whose linked pull request is closed or merged. gh is queried when it is available. A missing gh does not fail the command and does not select the workspace

options.name: orphaned
options.description: Select workspaces whose directory is missing, whose git registration is prunable, or whose branch ref is gone. A metadata record whose directory is already gone is dropped without deleting a directory git does not list

options.name: older-than
options.description: Select workspaces last used, or created when never used, at least this long ago. The value is a positive integer plus m (minutes), h, d, or w, such as 14d. Age alone does not remove another agent's workspace

options.name: owner
options.description: Only consider workspaces recorded for this owner. Unowned workspaces are excluded

options.name: keep-branch
options.description: Remove the workspace but keep its branch. Also implied by the keep-branch preference

options.name: no-hooks
options.description: Remove matching workspaces without running pre-delete hooks. This does not trust the repository. gc never asks for trust

options.name: json
options.description: Alias for --output json: one schema 2 envelope (schema, command, ok, data, warnings, error) on stdout. Progress and child output go to stderr

options.name: output
options.description: Output text or json. Overrides MABO_OUTPUT (text or json; empty means unset). --json is an alias for --output json

options.name: no-input
options.description: Never prompt for input. Also enabled by nonempty CI, JSON output, MABO_NO_INPUT other than empty or 0, or stdin/stderr without a TTY. MABO_AGENT_ID does not suppress prompts

examples.description: Show what would be removed
Remove merged, closed, and orphaned workspaces
Remove workspaces that have not been used for 14 days
Remove one agent's stale workspaces, including dirty ones

notes: gc is a dry run until --apply or --force. A second apply removes nothing
Removing the last workspace keeps the project directory and its repository marker so concurrent and subsequent creates can reuse it safely
gc selects linked workspaces inside the resolved workspaces directory and workspaces recorded in maboroshi/workspaces/<id>.json. An unrecorded workspace outside that directory is ignored

The current workspace, the primary checkout, and any workspace checked out on the default branch are never removed. The default branch is origin/HEAD when that ref exists, otherwise main, otherwise master
A branch that still points at the commit it was created from is not merged. It can still match --older-than or --orphaned

A stored pull request URL is passed to gh pr view. A number with no URL is checked only when gh can name the current repository. When gh is missing or cannot answer, gc reports that the pull request status is unavailable
Another agent's workspace is removed only when it is merged, its pull request is closed or merged, it is orphaned, or --owner names that agent
Dirty workspaces and workspaces with commits that are not on the default branch or a remote are skipped unless --force

Live removals run [hooks] pre-delete from .mabo.toml and then the same deletion as mabo delete. A hook failure marks that workspace failed and continues. Failures exit 6 if any persistent removal occurred, including when metadata cleanup fails after removal; otherwise they exit 1

gc never asks for trust. An untrusted repository with pre-delete hooks is skipped, and the detail is 'untrusted hooks'. --no-hooks removes those workspaces without running hooks. MABO_TRUST_ALL=1 trusts every repository for that process
--json lists each candidate, why it matched, and the action taken. The schema is documented in the README

MABO_TRUST_ALL=1 treats every repository as trusted for that process and does not write trust.toml. Set it to the single character 1. This is for CI and containers

examples.description: Clone owner/repo from github.com
Clone an SSH URL and check out a branch
Shallow clone and print the versioned JSON result
Fetch an existing checkout and register it

notes: owner/repo uses github.com. host/owner/repo uses that host.
https URLs, http URLs, ssh:// URLs, and scp-style git@host:owner/repo paths are accepted. A trailing .git suffix is optional.
The repository is placed at <root>/<host>/<owner>/<repo>. The host is lowercased, and a URL port is part of that directory (example.net:9443).

The root is the root key in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/maboroshi/config.toml, otherwise the first git config ghq.root value, otherwise $GHQ_ROOT, otherwise ~/ghq. A configured root is used without reading git config. A git config read failure warns and falls through to $GHQ_ROOT or ~/ghq.
When that path is already the same repository root, mabo registers it and prints the path instead of cloning again. --update fetches origin in that case.
remoteUrl omits http and https userinfo, including a token used as the username. ssh and scp-style URLs keep the login name. file:// URLs and absolute scp-style paths are rejected.
--branch and --depth apply only when cloning. updated is true only when an existing repository was fetched.
If the path exists but is not that repository, the command exits 2 with a usage error.

After clone or fetch, mabo registers the project. Registration failure exits 6 (partial) if a checkout was created or fetched, retaining path, cloned, updated, and the other result fields in data; otherwise it exits 1. Retrying can register the existing checkout. New workspaces for that repository are created under $XDG_DATA_HOME/maboroshi/workspaces/<checkout>-<hash> unless worktrees-directory is set.
Authentication is left to Git. mabo does not call gh.
Git progress is written to stderr. With --json, stdout is the schema 2 envelope; data contains: path, host, owner, repo, remoteUrl, cloned, and updated.
